title: No rules_version = '2'
msg: This file has no rules_version = '2' line, so Firebase evaluates it with version 1 semantics and the recursive wildcard behaves differently than the code you read.

title: allow ... : if true
msg: This path is open to anyone on the internet with your project ID — no sign-in, no rate limit, no audit trail.

title: Test-mode date still in the future
msg: Test mode: every document under this path is world readable and writable until the date in the rule.

title: Test-mode date already passed
msg: Test mode expired: every client read and write under this path is being denied, so the app is failing for real users.

title: Write on /{document=**}
msg: A write grant on the recursive wildcard applies to every collection in the database, including ones added after this file was written.

title: request.auth != null on a wildcard
msg: Any signed-in account reaches this whole subtree — anonymous auth and self-serve sign-up both count as signed in.

title: Owner segment never compared to request.auth.uid
msg: The path captures a user id but the condition never compares it to request.auth.uid, so one customer can write another customer's document.

title: Hard-coded uid in a rule
msg: A literal uid in the rules file is a permanent backdoor that survives role changes and is readable by anyone who downloads your rules.

title: Delete granted to any signed-in user
msg: Delete is granted on sign-in alone, so a single script can empty this collection and Firestore keeps no client-side undo.

title: read grants list as well as get
msg: read covers both get and list — a client can page the entire collection. Split into get and list if only single-document reads are intended.

title: Write with no field validation
msg: The condition checks who is writing but never what is written, so any client can add fields or change a price, role or balance.

title: Storage write with no size cap
msg: No request.resource.size check on a Storage write: one upload loop bills your project for as much egress and storage as it likes.

title: Storage write with no content-type check
msg: No request.resource.contentType check: a path meant for images will accept executables and HTML served from your own bucket domain.
